facts.statement: Tenant Perrin Dall reported on 4 Sep 2025 that the bathroom window will not open, the bedroom window will not secure and keys are missing at Unit 2, 18 Brindlewick Mews, Orellin ZZ1 1ZZ.

On the 9 Sep call the fault was clarified as opening-sash locks: bedroom sash opens but will not lock, bathroom sash is stuck with sticking locking buttons, kitchen sash works but has no key; the tenant also reported mould appearing in the bathroom.
The landlord authorised the agency to proceed with its own service provider on 4 Sep 2025; no spending limit or scope was stated, and no landlord spend cap is on file.
Hearthline Access (Tarin Vale) was instructed on 11 Sep and stood down the same day; the job was reassigned to Keypath Repairs (Edrin Moss) on 11 Sep.

No visit slot was ever confirmed: the tenant offered Thu 18 Sep 08:30-10:30 and consented to management-key access at any time; the provider never confirmed a time despite chasers on 14, 15 and 17 Sep.

On 17 Sep Edrin Moss said they had attended three times without finding the tenant in, had not collected management keys and could not give a date for doing so; no dates or times for the attempts were given.
On 22 and 25 Sep Edrin Moss said the work was completed on Fri 19 Sep and promised an invoice; as at 25 Sep no invoice, confirmed appointment, visit notes or other attendance evidence exists on file.
Tarin Vale (Hearthline, untrusted) claims the tenant was 'happy with a date and time' but gives no date, time or written confirmation; no appointment is recorded in the voicemail of 11 Sep either.
No priced quote has been produced or approved by the landlord at any point in this case.

Dear Perrin Dall,

Re: Unit 2, 18 Brindlewick Mews — window sash locks and missing key.

I am sorry for how long this has taken. The contractor, Keypath Repairs, has told us by phone that work was carried out at the property on Friday 19 September, but we have no visit record, photographs or invoice from them, so we cannot treat the job as finished until you confirm. Please could you tell us:

1. Has anyone attended the flat to work on the window locks? If so, roughly when?
2. Do the bedroom and bathroom sashes now lock and open properly, and have you been given a key for the kitchen sash?

If nobody has attended, please say so and we will arrange a new visit. Your note that a contractor may attend at any time using management keys while you are at work is on file (your emails of 11 and 14 September) and we will use that. There is no confirmed appointment in place at the moment, so please do not wait in for anyone.

Separately, you mentioned mould in the bathroom on our call of 9 September. While we deal with this: please keep the bathroom door closed and the extractor fan running during and after showers or baths, wipe surface moisture from the window and sills, leave a gap between furniture and external walls, and wipe affected areas with a proprietary mould cleaner following the label. If the bathroom sash still will not open, tell us — ventilation matters and we will include it in the works. Please send photographs of the affected area and tell us how large it is and whether it is getting worse, and tell us straight away if anyone in the household has a breathing condition, so we can prioritise it correctly.

I will come back to you as soon as the contractor responds; I have asked them for evidence of attendance and their invoice by Monday 29 September.
